decision: Buy one SPY 2026-12-11 755 call at the 1.26 ask (US$126.65, 12.7% of equity) with a resting take-profit at 6.30 (5x) and no nightly stop. The analyst's case passed its entry test (EV 1.54 per dollar at 26% vol); the red team could not refute it but cut the estimate to about 1.1 (90% CI 0.55-1.83) and showed the edge comes from rebounds after drawdowns, so this is a marginal rebound bet sized at one contract. The 12-04 742 call was rejected (EV about 0.9).

research.analyst: Calendar-day IV overstates the gap to realized; only the upside call wing is cheap. Central vol 26% (trading days) with 1 point lower per +1% rally, zero drift, fat tails: SPY 12-11 755C x1 with take-profit 6.30: EV 1.54 per dollar (1.39 at 25%, 0.87 at implied); SPY 12-04 742C: 1.20 (0.87 at implied). research.red_team: Vol fades after shocks: after similar set-ups the next 11 sessions realized a median 24% (0.82x the 20-day figure), so a 23-24% central vol is better supported; at that level A is 1.16-1.29 and B 0.88-0.98. No material code bugs (take-profit marked at mid flatters a few percent). De-duplicated episodes 2021-26 (n=27, 5-10% below the 20-day high): the 11-session high reached +5.3% in 22%; backtest EV for A 1.10 (90% CI 0.55-1.83), B 0.91; unconditional days only 0.44. The edge is a rebound bet; 2 of 13 bear-market episodes paid. Verdict: accept A marginally at one contract, reject B.

actions.thesis: Cheap upside wing after a 7% drawdown: implied 19% (trading days) against an expected 23-26% realized, spanning the 12-08/09 FOMC. Marginal rebound bet, EV about 1.1 per dollar per the red team; one contract, held to expiry unless the 6.30 take-profit fills.
